findings.title: getClientsWithPermission can never return per-client grants and returns the type name "Clients" instead
findings.body: `findByType(server, "Clients", ...)` only matches resources whose type is set. The per-client resources that `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` creates (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:104-110) never call `setType`. Only the type-level resource built in `init` (AdminPermissionsSchema.java:249-250) has type `Clients`, and its name is `Clients`. So this method skips every per-client permission. When an all-clients permission matches, it puts the literal string "Clients" into the set where a client id should go. Nothing in `services/src/main/java` calls `getClientsWithPermission` today, so nothing breaks yet, but the first caller will get wrong results. Two fixes would work: set the type when `getOrCreateResource` creates a resource, or filter out the type resource and look the resources up another way.

findings.title: With V2 on, deleting a client no longer cleans up its V2 resource and permissions
findings.body: `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` and `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` are versions 1 and 2 of the same feature (Profile.java:56,58), so only one can be on at a time. With V2 on, the new guard skips `ClientRemovedEvent` entirely. That avoids the `UnsupportedOperationException` from `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled` (ClientPermissionsV2.java:193-195). It also means nothing removes the resource named after the deleted client's id in the admin-permissions client, or the scope permissions that point to it. Those entries stay in the permissions UI and REST API after the client is gone. Is this cleanup planned somewhere else, for example in `ClientApplicationSynchronizer`, the way users are handled?

findings.title: Dead code: getEvaluationContext, logger and the TOKEN_EXCHANGE import are never used
findings.body: Nothing calls `getEvaluationContext` (token exchange throws `UnsupportedOperationException` at line 149). The `logger` at line 51 and the static import of `TOKEN_EXCHANGE` at line 46 are also unused, along with the `Scope`, `EvaluationContext`, `ClientModelIdentity` and `DefaultEvaluationContext` imports that only exist for that method.

findings.title: Javadoc on void require* methods says "Returns true"
findings.body: `requireView()` (line 96-98) and `requireViewClientScopes()` (line 100-103) return `void` and throw `ForbiddenException`. Their new Javadoc says "Returns `true` if ...". It should say "Throws ForbiddenException if ... returns `false`", like the other `require*` docs.

summary:
**Batch 1 of 2.** I found nothing in part 1 that should block the merge, but there are four things to consider. I read all nine files in this part.

- **`getClientsWithPermission` is wrong but has no callers.** It looks up resources by the type `Clients`, but the per-client resources are created without a type. It can therefore never find a per-client grant. When an all-clients permission matches, it returns the literal name "Clients" where a client id should be.
- **Deleted clients leave V2 permissions behind (open question).** The new feature guard in the client-removed listener stops a V2 crash. It also means nothing cleans up a deleted client's V2 resource or the permissions that point to it. I couldn't find where that cleanup would happen, so I've asked the author.
- **Dead code in `ClientPermissionsV2`:** the token-exchange evaluation-context helper, the logger and several imports are unused.
- **Javadoc wording:** on two `void` require methods it says "Returns true" when they actually throw.

The V2 permission checks for manage, configure, view and role mapping match the V1 structure and the new tests.

**Batch 2 of 2.** I found no problems in this part. UserResourceTypePermissionTest.java has one change: every call now uses the static helpers getScopePermissionsResource(client) and createPermission(client, permission) from AbstractPermissionTest. Each call passes the test's own injected admin-permissions `client` field, so it hits the same endpoint the old helpers did. The 201 CREATED check still runs, and the new overloads can't be mixed up with the other createPermission signatures. The resource counts in testDelete still pass after the schema changes elsewhere in this PR, because the test reads the expected number from AdminPermissionsSchema.SCHEMA at run time.
